answers.answer: Honest read: the reject-willingness gate is real but it is primarily an UPSTREAM gate, and I must say so rather than pretend a cash-trapped micro-brand can casually reject a fully-landed lot. My spec sequences QC cheapest-first NOW and starts QC 'as a number in the purchase order, not on a machine' — the enforceable teeth are (a) the numeric PO thresholds the SUPPLIER must hit (CVm%/IPI <=25% USTER, ICI >=3-4 post-wash, composition tolerance), with pass thresholds 'written into the PO so the supplier shares the risk', and (b) PPS/pre-production-sample approval BEFORE bulk yarn money is committed. That is where a failing ICI grade is caught cheaply and where rejection is economically executable — the supplier bears the sunk cost, not the brand. For a landed A2 lot that fails the ICI post-wash gate AFTER weeks of ocean freight, the incoming AQL inspection I OWN still produces an accept/reject decision [FACT: capability 'run the incoming AQL garment inspection'], but the ECONOMIC feasibility of eating the sunk landed cost is NOT my call — it turns on the working-capital position, which the DECISION_MEMO calls the modal death (gate G3, [UNKNOWN]/UNSIZED). Per my boundaries I give 'no individualized... contract-law counsel' and route viability/cash questions to the proper authority: whether the brand can afford to reject a landed lot defers to unit_economics + the DECISION_MEMO (dominance rule: viability -> unit_economics). So the correct statement is: front-load rejection to the PO thresholds and PPS gate where the supplier is on the hook; the OWNED landed AQL gate still decides accept/reject on quality, but its economic executability at the landed stage is bounded by G3 and deferred, not asserted. Presenting the landed reject as unconditionally executable would be an over-claim my spec does not support without that deferral.

answers.answer: Honest limits on the duty-guard claim, staying in my lane. What the composition +/- tolerance genuinely does: it makes the care label, the yarn cert, and the HTS 6110 line MATCH the actual fibre content, so the declared composition is what shipped — a misdeclaration guard. What it does NOT automatically solve, and where I over-claim if I am not careful: the chief-weight rule flips the duty HEADING at the 50/50 boundary (cotton 6110.20.20 ~16.5% vs acrylic/MMF 6110.30.30 ~32% [FACT trio; wool 6110.11 ~16%]; never the discredited ~7% cotton figure). A blend whose target sits NEAR that chief-weight cliff could drift inside my +/- tolerance and still cross the boundary — e.g. a nominal 52/48 cotton-major lot drifting to 49/51 stays within a +/-3 composition tolerance yet flips the chief weight and therefore the heading and the duty rate. So the tolerance does NOT by itself guarantee duty-heading stability for cliff-adjacent blends; the correct QC-side move is to design blends AWAY from the 50/50 chief-weight cliff (a comfortable margin so tolerance drift cannot cross it) and to flag cliff-adjacent designs. Crucially, the DUTY CONSEQUENCE and the classification are NOT mine to rule on — per my boundaries I give 'no individualized... customs-classification advice' and route the heading/duty ruling to unit_economics (dominance: landed cost/duty/heading 6110/chief-weight cliff/IOR -> unit_economics_strategist). My deliverable is the composition-match guard + the flag that a cliff-adjacent blend needs unit_economics to confirm the heading; asserting the tolerance 'solves' duty misclassification, or stating the duty consequence myself, would be over-claim + a lane cross.
answers.grounded_in: capability 'write the contractual yarn spec' (composition tolerance as duty guard); competency_questions_covered ('fibre-composition clause double as customs-duty-misdeclaration guard'); boundaries 'no individualized... customs-classification advice'; router dominance 'landed cost/duty/chief-weight cliff -> unit_economics'; router N5 (cotton ~16.5% not ~7%)
answers.specialist_supports_note: partial: the spec correctly frames the tolerance as a MISDECLARATION guard (label matches yarn) and correctly routes duty rulings out of lane, but it does not explicitly note the chief-weight-cliff limit — that a tolerance-compliant lot can still cross the 50/50 heading boundary — nor the 'design blends away from the cliff' consequence.
answers.gap_note: SCOPE/precision (matches R1 Q3 watch, sharpened): the duty-guard is honestly a composition-MATCH guard, not a chief-weight-cliff guard; the spec should state that a +/- tolerance does not protect a cliff-adjacent blend from a heading flip, that the fix is designing away from 50/50, and that the classification/duty consequence defers to unit_economics. Duty trio stated correctly (~16.5%/~16%/~32%), no ~7%. No fabrication. Disposition: apply_now (add the chief-weight-cliff caveat + explicit unit_economics deferral).
